docs.markdown:
# 0.10.8 preparation audit

Date: 2026-09-25. Starting revision: `5db995a` (0.10.7), clean checkout, CI
green, `pnpm audit` clean.

Method: six parallel read-only reviews (deploy engine; route authorization in
the less-audited modules; client ↔ server contract across web, SDK, CLI and
MCP; lib/plugins/retention/migrations; node agent, installer, CI and the
template catalog; web UI correctness). Every candidate was re-confirmed against
the code before fixing. Each fix carries a regression test that was run against
the pre-fix source (old file written back with `git show`, never a stash) and
seen to fail. Defect ids r260–r362.

Validation: the serialized release gate (`pnpm release:check` — typecheck,
lint, build, every workspace test suite with coverage floors) passes on the
release tree. Not exercised end to end: real remote nodes, the installer on a
live host (the tty guard and the EXIT trap were exercised in a container and
with a fake `systemctl`), and real-browser flows.

## Fixed

| Area | Id | Fault | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| API tokens | r260 | `parseId` accepted `1e0`/`0x1`/`+1`, the sub-resource scope overrides matched only `\d+` — a services-only token reached env, webhooks and deploys | Canonical decimal ids only; overrides match any id segment |
| Authorization | r280 | Members could delete operator exec/backup jobs; viewers read exec commands and output | Operator-only delete, 404 on miss; command/output redacted for non-operators |
| Authorization | r281 | `GET /alerts` listed every tenant's rules | Filtered to visible services; host-wide rules for operators |
| Authorization | r285 | Tag PUT stripped other workspaces' labels | Invisible labels are preserved |
| Authorization | r287 | Any drain (disabled, other service's) usable by non-operators, spending its API key | Enabled global or same-service drains only |
| Audit trail | r282, r283, r286 | Env overwrite, service export (plaintext secrets), metric flush, build-cache store skipped `audit()` | Audited; marketplace refresh operator-only; plugin inspect no longer invents telemetry |
| Secrets | r284 | Applying a config preset rewrote an ad-hoc secret as plaintext | Secrecy resolved from the existing row |
| Secrets | r310 | Egress refusals echoed the full URL (webhook tokens) into logs and `notification_log` | Origin only |
| Deploy engine | r272 | Cancel + redeploy ran two pipelines in one checkout | Worker waits for the cancelled pipeline to exit |
| Deploy engine | r273 | A failed `git pull` (force-push) was swallowed and the old HEAD deployed green | Checkout moves to the fetched remote tip; real failures fail the deploy |
| Deploy engine | r274, r274b | The generated `nixpacks.toml` froze later manifest changes | Marked, regenerated or removed per deploy; pre-marker files recognised as untracked |
| Deploy engine | r321 | Docker services never mounted their attached volumes | One `-v` per attachment |
| Data loss | r275, r277 | Container/volume file editors silently truncated files over 1 MiB to their tail, then saved it | Refused with 413 |
| Backups | r276 | A failed backup left the plaintext dump on disk and in the container | Cleaned on every failure path |
| Backups | r312 | A 200 `CompleteMultipartUpload` carrying `<Error>` recorded a phantom remote recovery point | Treated as failure, upload aborted |
| Concurrency | r314 | Two waiters could both take a stale cross-process lock; release deleted others' locks | Ownership token; rename-based stale takeover |
| Webhooks | r313 | Replay guard keyed on the unsigned delivery-id header | Also dedupes sha256(body) per service |
| Remote nodes | r264–r270 | Published-port redeploys always failed; crash loops passed health; cmd/socket/volumes dropped silently; multi-line env and `_KEY` rejected; changed repo URL ignored; credentialed repos and DB templates deployed broken; tags recorded as digests | Fixed or refused up front with a reason (`lib/remoteDeploy.ts`) |
| Database | r300 | `services.environment_id` and `backups.destination_id` had no `ON DELETE SET NULL` in SQL — lane and destination deletes 500'd | Migration 0064 rebuilds both tables; drift test now compares foreign keys |
| Database | r301 | Revoke → re-invite the same email 500'd on a full unique index | Partial unique index (outstanding invites only) |
| Retention | r302 | `backup_drills`, `workspace_invitations`, `domain_transfers`, `cache_registry_blobs` unswept; running deploys' logs pruned; drill plaintext left behind | Sweeps added; live logs kept; leftovers removed |
| Scheduling | r303 | A disabled job kept firing up to 5 minutes | Scheduled runs re-check `enabled` |
| Images | r311 | "In use" compared image references with ids — always false | Resolves container image ids |
| Installer | r261–r263 | ACME prompt aborted tty-less self-updates after stopping the panel; failed upgrades left the panel stopped; `--docker` could never pass its image check and ignored `--version` | Real tty probe; EXIT trap restarts the unit; lowercase image, pinned `:vX.Y.Z` |
| Templates | r320, r330 | wud mounted a volume where the Docker socket belongs; speedtest-tracker lacked APP_KEY; community templates 404'd on open/deploy | Fixed |
| Contract | r331–r335, r340–r347 | Stale PgBouncer responses; no domain verify in SDK/CLI/web; MCP scopes that could never pass; SDK types that disagreed with the server; PATCH silently dropping tag fields; Web Studio link to a loopback port; clearing a volume mount ignored; stale caches after saves; unpaginated Activity; no way to set a deployment lane | Fixed |
| Web UI | r290–r299 | Log autoscroll trap, repeating update toast, keyboard-inaccessible Hub cards and dialogs, focus not restored, invite landing in the wrong workspace, stale env table, stale analysis, doubled log lines | Fixed |
| Test hygiene | — | Two suites booted the real Traefik plugin, recreating the host's `ninedeploy-traefik` container on a developer machine; the webhook suite called the real builders (`docker stop/rm`, `compose down`, a PM2 daemon that outlived the run) | Stubbed |
| Proxy | r350 | A Traefik container serving another data dir's config matched the fingerprint and was kept | Mount source compared too |
| Tenancy | r351 (was r096b) | A new service under a deleted service's slug mounted its retained data volume | 409 `slug_volume_retained` on every create path |
| Compose | r352 | A repo-committed `.env` was replaced by panel values, then deleted | Panel values layered on top, original restored |
| Fan-out | r353 | Extra nodes cloned credentialed repos anonymously, with no egress gate | Skipped with a log line; gate added |
| SSO | r354 | SAML could never sign anyone in, yet providers could be created | Refused with `saml_unavailable` |
| Egress | r355 (was r099b) | DNS rebinding between the git egress check and git's own resolution | `http.curloptResolve` pinned to the vetted addresses (https) |
| Backups | r356 | Drills used host tools no installer provides and could not read Mongo archives | In-image checks, completion trailers, `unverifiable` status |
| Installer | r357, r362 | A failed tarball upgrade left the panel down; `db:migrate` migrated a stray database | Rollback to the previous release (DB restored when migrated); relative DB path anchored at the repo root |
| Panel | r358–r361 | Transfer accept link 404; enrolment token unreachable; branding invisible; 404/403 existence leak | Pages/cards added; uniform 404 |

Dependencies: fastify 5.12.5, @fastify/static 10.1.4, @fastify/websocket
11.3.1, jose 6.2.12, pm2 7.0.4, MCP SDK 1.30.1, TanStack Query 5.103.2,
xyflow 12.11.6.

## Behaviour changes operators may notice

- Migration 0064 rebuilds the `services` and `backups` tables (foreign keys
  off, ids and AUTOINCREMENT counters preserved). The installer's pre-upgrade
  database backup covers it.
- Deploy checkouts now reset to the remote branch tip (`checkout -f`): local
  edits inside the panel's working copies are discarded on every deploy.
- Node-pinned services that need a template command, the Docker socket, extra
  volumes, a Git credential or a managed database are now refused with a
  reason instead of deploying broken. Upgrade node agents to pick up
  `_`-prefixed env keys and repository-URL changes.
- Route ids must be canonical decimals (`01`, `1e0` → 400). `PATCH
  /v1/services/:id` answers 400 `tags_via_put` for tag fields.
- Plugin inspect reports `null` for runtime counters the kernel does not
  track.

## Known, not fixed in this release

- SAML sign-in (r354 refuses it): needs a vetted XML-signature library and an
  AuthnRequest bound to `InResponseTo` + a RelayState cookie.
- ssh / git:// remotes are egress-checked but not DNS-pinned; node-side
  (`git.ensure`) clones re-resolve on the node.
- Remote compose still overwrites a repo's `.env` on the node (agent
  protocol unchanged in a patch).
- Compose-stack named volumes (`ndcmp-<slug>_*`) outlive a deleted stack and
  are not covered by the r351 slug check.
- The upgrade rollback (r357) protects upgrades started by this installer
  onward; a health-gate failure after the restart is not rolled back
  automatically (the rollback folder is kept and named).
- Some branding fields (`primaryColor`, `footerHtml`) are not applied —
  footer HTML would need a sanitiser.
- r094b is closed by refusal: TOTP users cannot sign in through OIDC (they
  use password + code); a pending-2FA step would let them.
- Wave 4 of the 2026-09 security plan (host/supply chain) has not started.

docs.title: CI on your own runners
docs.description: The complete upstream guide to ci on your own runners, synchronized with the product repository.
docs.markdown:
# CI jobs on your own runners (R5)

NineDeploy can run a service's tests or build steps on machines you enrol as **runners**. A pipeline is a container image and a shell script. A job is one run of the pipeline at a commit.

The panel keeps every job and every attempt in its database. Runners pull work over HTTPS with their own token; the panel never connects to them.

In the panel, a service's **CI** tab holds its pipeline, its jobs and each attempt's log, and **Settings → CI runners** enrols runners. The SDK exposes the same through `client.ci`, and the CLI through `ninedeploy ci`:

```sh
ninedeploy ci runners add builder-1 --labels linux,x64 --capacity 2   # prints the token once
ninedeploy ci runners list
ninedeploy ci set web pipeline.json          # the JSON body shown below
ninedeploy ci run web --ref main --follow    # exits non-zero unless the job succeeds
ninedeploy ci jobs web
ninedeploy ci log web 12 --follow
ninedeploy ci approve web 12                 # or: cancel
```

## Enrolling a runner

An operator creates the runner in **Settings → CI runners**, or with the API, and receives its token once (`ndrun_…`). Only the token's hash is stored.

```sh
curl -X POST https://panel.example.com/v1/ci/runners \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $OPERATOR_TOKEN" -H 'content-type: application/json' \
  -d '{"name":"builder-1","labels":["linux","x64"],"capacity":2}'
```

On the runner machine, start the panel image's runner with Docker. The work directory must be mounted **at the same path** on the host, because the job containers' bind mounts are resolved by the host's Docker:

```sh
docker run -d --name ninedeploy-ci-runner --restart unless-stopped \
  -v /var/run/docker.sock:/var/run/docker.sock \
  -v /var/lib/ninedeploy-runner:/var/lib/ninedeploy-runner \
  -e NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_WORKDIR=/var/lib/ninedeploy-runner \
  -e NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_URL=https://panel.example.com \
  -e NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_TOKEN=ndrun_… \
  -e NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_CAPACITY=2 \
  ghcr.io/ninedeploy/ninedeploy:v<panel version> node apps/server/dist/ciRunner.js
```

| Variable | Default | Meaning |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_CAPACITY` | 1 | Jobs run at the same time. The panel also checks this against the runner's recorded capacity. |
| `NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_MEMORY` | `2g` | Memory limit of each job container. |
| `NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_CPUS` | `2` | CPU limit of each job container. |
| `NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_PIDS` | 1024 | Process limit of each job container. |
| `NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_WORKDIR` | the system temp directory | Where job workspaces are created. |
| `NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_NETWORK` | `isolated` | `isolated`: each job gets a bridge network of its own. `none`: jobs get no network at all (no package downloads either). |

`DELETE /v1/ci/runners/:id` revokes a runner:

- its token stops working at once;
- jobs it was running are requeued;
- at its next heartbeat it is refused and kills them.

`GET /v1/ci/runners` lists every runner with its labels, capacity, online state (seen within 90 s) and running attempts.

## A service's pipeline

A service admin sets the pipeline (`PUT /v1/services/:id/ci`):

```json
{
  "image": "node:24-alpine",
  "script": "npm ci\nnpm test",
  "labels": ["linux"],
  "secrets": ["NPM_TOKEN"],
  "timeoutMinutes": 30,
  "maxAttempts": 2,
  "requireApproval": false,
  "runOnPush": true,
  "gateDeploys": false
}
```

| Field | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `script` | Runs with `sh -e` in `/workspace`. |
| `labels` | A runner must carry every one of them to take the job. |
| `secrets` | Names of **service variables** the job receives as environment. Nothing else from the service reaches it, and a PR preview receives none. Setting the pipeline is admin-only for this reason. |
| `maxAttempts` | Total tries when a runner is **lost** mid-job. A script that fails is not retried. |
| `requireApproval` | Holds every job until a service admin approves it (`POST …/ci/jobs/:jobId/approve`). Runners see nothing before that. |
| `runOnPush` | A push to the service branch runs a job at the pushed commit (see below). |
| `gateDeploys` | Every deploy waits for a job at its commit and builds only what the job passed (see below). |

Members run the pipeline with `POST /v1/services/:id/ci/jobs` and an optional `{ "ref": "<branch or commit>" }`; the service branch is used by default. A job copies the pipeline when it is created, so later edits never change it.

`GET /v1/services/:id/ci/jobs/:jobId` shows the job with its attempts: runner, status and exit code.

`GET …/attempts/:number/log?offset=<bytes>` reads the log from that byte on:

- it answers `{ "data": "…", "size": 1234, "done": false }`: ask again with `offset=size` for what came after, until `done` is true (the panel's CI tab follows a log this way);
- the log is capped at 8 MiB per attempt;
- on a protected lane, only the lane's admins can read it.

Finished jobs and their logs are removed after 30 days.

## Jobs on push

With `runOnPush`, a verified push webhook for the service branch runs a job at the pushed commit:

- a `[skip ci]` or `[skip cd]` marker in the head commit skips the job as it skips the deploy;
- a job runs even when watch paths skip the deploy;
- a replayed delivery for a commit that already has a push job adds none;
- the webhook's answer names the job (`ciJobId`).

When the pipeline also has `gateDeploys`, the push adds no job of its own: the deploy it queues runs one.

## Deploys gated on CI

With `gateDeploys`, every deploy of the service waits in **`awaiting_ci`** until a job passes, whatever queued it: a push, the UI, the API, a schedule or a rollback.

1. When the deploy reaches the front of the queue, the panel creates a job at the deploy's commit (or at the branch head when the deploy names none). The job is linked to the deploy, and the deploy holds no build slot while it waits.
2. The job checks out the source and pins the commit it tested.
3. When the job passes, the deploy gets that commit and is queued again. The build checks out exactly that commit, and the pipeline refuses to build any other.
4. When the job fails or is cancelled, the deploy fails with the job's error.

More rules:

- Cancelling a waiting deploy, or replacing it with a newer one, cancels its job.
- An approval given before the commit was known is cleared, as with the GitHub workflow gate.
- When the service also requires GitHub workflows, the NineDeploy job runs first and the GitHub check then verifies the commit the job pinned.
- **PR previews** of the service are gated by the same pipeline. Their jobs get none of the service's variables. A job for a pull request from a **fork** waits for a service admin to approve it before any runner sees fork code. A fork preview deploy that names no commit fails instead: the approval would otherwise cover whatever the fork branch holds when a runner fetches it. Redeploy it from the pull request.
- Removing the pipeline, or turning `gateDeploys` off, lets waiting deploys through at the next check.

## What a job sees, and what it doesn't

The runner fetches the source from the panel (`GET /v1/ci/runner/attempts/:id/source`):

- The panel checks it out with the service's own Git credential, or uses the uploaded source archive.
- It sends the files as a tar.gz **without `.git`**, so the credential in the remote URL never leaves the panel.
- The first checkout pins the commit on the job, so a retry builds the same tree.
- The job sees the commit as `NINEDEPLOY_CI_COMMIT`, with `CI=true`, `NINEDEPLOY_CI_JOB` and `NINEDEPLOY_CI_ATTEMPT`.

The job container:

- gets `/workspace` and the variables the pipeline names;
- runs with `no-new-privileges` and the memory, CPU and process limits above;
- is removed when it ends;
- never gets the Docker socket, the runner token or its lease token.

Variable values reach Docker through the client's environment, not its command line.

Some names would change the runner's own Docker client rather than the job, so the pipeline refuses them as `secrets`:
- `PATH`, `HOME`, `LD_*`, `DYLD_*`
- `DOCKER_*`, `BUILDKIT_*`, `NODE_*`
- the proxy and CA variables
- `BASH_ENV`, `ENV`, `IFS`, `CI`, `NINEDEPLOY_*` and similar

The panel and the runner drop such a name again before a job starts.

Each job runs on a Docker bridge network of its own (`nd-ci-net-<attempt>`), removed with the job:

- it cannot reach other containers on the runner machine by their address, nor another job;
- it can still reach the internet, the runner machine itself (and ports published on it) and whatever the machine's network reaches.

So use a dedicated machine for runners and keep production networks out of its reach. With `NINEDEPLOY_RUNNER_NETWORK=none`, jobs have no network at all.

Each running job takes one of Docker's bridge address pools. A default Docker installation has about 30, shared with everything else on the machine, so keep a runner's capacity well below that or widen `default-address-pools` in the Docker daemon's configuration. When a runner starts, it removes the job networks it left behind. It also removes any job network that has been empty for more than ten minutes, including one left by a runner whose token has since changed.

## Recovery

All of a job's state lives in the panel's database.

| Event | What happens |
| --- | --- |
| Two runners ask for the same job | A conditional update gives it to one; the other gets nothing. |
| A runner reports | Each attempt has a 60-second **lease** that the runner renews every 15 s. Every report carries the attempt's lease token, which is bound to that runner. |
| A runner disappears | It crashes, loses its network or is killed. Its lease lapses, the attempt is marked **lost**, and the job is requeued, or failed once `maxAttempts` is used up. When that runner comes back, its heartbeat answers `stop`, its result is refused (409), and it removes the containers it left when it restarts. **A job can't be counted as succeeded twice.** |
| A job is cancelled | Its runner kills the container at its next heartbeat. A late result does not count. |
| The panel restarts | Every live lease gets a fresh period, so runners that could not report while the panel was down are not declared lost. Log chunks are numbered and retried for about five minutes, so the log keeps its order and loses no lines. |

The runner protocol is described in the API document under the `ci` tag (`/v1/ci/runner/claim`, `…/heartbeat`, `…/log`, `…/finish`, `…/source`).

## Verified

On Docker 28 in an isolated dind, with a public repository as the source:

- **Successful job:** the source arrived at a pinned commit without `.git`, and the named secret arrived. The container had no Docker socket and no runner token, and it was removed afterwards.
- **Failing script:** it exited 3, failed the job and was not retried.
- **Cancel during a run:** the container was gone 13 s later.
- **Runner killed with SIGKILL:** its container kept running. 61 s later the lease lapsed and the job was requeued. The restarted runner removed the orphaned container and finished attempt 2. Attempt 1 stayed lost.
- **Panel down for 70 s, longer than a lease, during a job:** after the restart, attempt 1 finished with its whole log in order.

The deploy gate, with the same runner in dind and the gate functions the worker calls:

- a deploy queued without a commit waited in `awaiting_ci`, and the build guard refused it;
- when its job passed, the deploy was queued again at the job's commit (`7fd1a60b01f9`), the guard accepted it and no second job ran;
- the job ran on its own network (default route via 172.19.0.1, not the default bridge's 172.17.0.1);
- a job exiting 4 failed its deploy with "CI job #2 failed: Exited with 4";
- cancelling a waiting deploy cancelled its job: the container was gone 14 s later, and no job network was left.

Job networks, on Docker 28 with a listener in a container on the default bridge:

- a container on the default bridge (where jobs ran before) reached it;
- a container on a job network could not, yet reached the internet;
- with `none`, a container could not even resolve a name.

docs.markdown:
# Competitive delivery work

Baseline: NineDeploy 0.17.1, main abf5a39a. This is an implementation and acceptance tracker, not a statement of competitor parity.

Latest recovery work, 2026-11-03: the internal PostgreSQL restore/query adapter passed [real hosted acceptance 41649048270](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41649048270) on frozen source `608fe3f094d952d0aff4b9073a340e2d708b2bee`. Plain/custom dumps restored the known earlier data after the source changed; wrong data, invalid SQL and a missing extension were refused. Independent receipts confirm source/backup preservation and owned cleanup. Local covering checks passed 91 tests in four files, server typecheck and lint. Public drill integration, other engines, PostgreSQL PITR and final full-source certification remain required. See [Isolated restore verification](RESTORE_VERIFICATION.md).

Latest Swarm evidence, 2026-11-06: the Swarm support matrix ([DEPLOYMENTS.md §7](DEPLOYMENTS.md)) passed [hosted acceptance 42238384185](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/42238384185) on `abd8eb45`, a real two-task Swarm service, with [main CI 42238365115](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/42238365115) green on the same commit. Logs came from both tasks in time order; Stop → 0/0 and Restart → 2/2 with the route serving again; a service scaled to 0 outside the panel was brought back to 2/2 by the runtime patrol; inspect and the File Browser reached a task on the panel host; stats showed the per-task 128 MiB limit (tasks averaged); a 404 health path read healthy; `Container running` readiness deployed a service whose port answers nothing; a Swarm service removed behind the panel's back was marked `error`. Volume attachment (422 `swarm_unsupported`), TCP readiness (400), sleep (400 `cannot_sleep`) and autoscaling (no metric) were refused. This closes the R2 "Remaining Swarm support" gate. Still out of scope: metrics of tasks on worker nodes (the panel host's tasks only), distributed workers and Swarm autoscaling, which is not offered.

Earlier Swarm evidence, 2026-11-03: the [single-manager artifact/restart cohort](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41644236264) passed on frozen source `1e2214e3ae765e1d414f89149649abb9c38bfee1`. Independent verification counted 13,174 exact application HTTP 200 responses with no errors/502 across Docker-to-Swarm migration, pinned promotion after repository HEAD advanced, readiness-held panel restart recovery and recorded rollback. Native/image/commit identities and owned cleanup passed. Its dedicated integration gate, distributed workers, other failure timings and final release certification remain open; see [Swarm runtime acceptance](SWARM_RUNTIME_ACCEPTANCE.md). PR #25 remains the only open integration PR while its full source/image CI finishes.

Latest node evidence, 2026-11-03: [run 41607197631](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41607197631) passed automatic panel retirement with 1,099 verified waking pages and no 502/connection errors; its fixture seeds dormant state. Subsequent [run 41616036959](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41616036959) passed real five-minute idle per service, concurrent Stop, held strict HTTP readiness, new-process recovery, guarded demand and Stop during wake: 2,328 valid responses and owned cleanup. PRs #15–#18 and #22 are merged; #22 passed full source/runtime CI. The next [public manual-wake comparison](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41622507659) reproduced wrong-host Docker mutation before the fix, then passed with the same-name panel decoy untouched and 675 valid responses, no 502/connection errors. Its API/worker are real; sleep admission is a private real-observation factory. PR #23 passed full CI and merged to main as 9e79b931. The later [real lost-routing-acknowledgement cohort](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41627779632) restored the healthy application before any Stop, with 640 valid responses, no 502/connection errors and owned cleanup. PR #24 also passed full CI and merged. The later [public automatic cycle](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41634736108) passed normal API/plugin timers, a genuine traffic reset, automatic sleep/wake, readiness hold and panel restart with 791 valid responses and settled audit events. That public candidate passed all required source/runtime and serving-traffic checks on `65d15f69f71eb0e63e59dd1600e7455089e331a8` and merged through PR #25 as `977390d7279268b3ab8dffd0dde133fa40668c01`; it remains unreleased. Never-bound orphan collection, other fault timings and the wider R2–R6/final release scope remain open; see [NODE_SLEEP_WAKE.md](NODE_SLEEP_WAKE.md) for frozen sources and exact validation boundaries.

Development checkpoint, 2026-11-03: node RPS autoscaling has hosted 1→2→1 and source-loss acceptance ([CI 41464316996](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41464316996)); see [NODE_RPS_AUTOSCALING.md](NODE_RPS_AUTOSCALING.md) for the exact source and scope. [Node sleep/wake](NODE_SLEEP_WAKE.md) remains incomplete: agent idle watches and the wake catcher exist, and the panel's read-only 15-second scheduler, bound transport and conservative continuous idle proof passed [source/runtime CI 41524700096](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41524700096) before PR #11 merged. The durable sleep/wake authority foundation passed [full source/runtime CI 41538310932](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41538310932) before PR #12 merged. Fallback routing and permission-bound publication passed [CI 41538382781](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41538382781) before PR #13 merged. The internal wake controller passed [CI 41538384727](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41538384727) before PR #14 merged. Subsequent sleep, polling and maintenance recovery remain under feature acceptance; automatic node sleep stays disabled. Public capability/status reporting, non-disruptive catcher replacement and hosted sleep/wake traffic acceptance remain open. These development results do not certify the full R2–R6 scope or a new release.

Current published release: **[0.18.21](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/releases/tag/v0.18.21)** (`d5664149699a8cfc614ca3f7303950a9b6af900e`), which completes R3. R4 and R5 shipped in 0.18.15, and R6's desktop source is in that release too; its installers are not published yet. Next feature release: **0.19.0 (R2: remaining runtime support)**. Validated maintenance fixes keep shipping as patch releases between feature releases. The paragraphs below about 0.18.16 and earlier record those releases as they were.

Published increment **0.18.16** fixes local Docker primary-network readiness and includes seven additional version-pinned Hub blueprints. Resolve the configured primary network by name/full ID, preserve legacy default/bridge compatibility, refuse missing or invalid addresses, pin explicit HTTP/TCP probes to that address and require the address to remain unchanged afterward. Command readiness inherits the corrected TCP gate. Running-mode policy and node-agent RPC operands are unchanged. This increment does not complete R2–R6; desktop installers remain a separate unsigned acceptance track and signed macOS credential persistence is not certified.

The [0.18.16 release workflow](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41304221842) completed successfully on attempt 1: full release gate, backup integration, signed multi-architecture image, all seven versioned-image smoke cohorts, promotion and all five npm publications. [Exact-source CI](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41304226265) passed 17,788 tests in 1,125 files plus Docker/runtime and real Docker/PostgreSQL integration. The release gate also ran all eight test tasks; four build dependencies were cached. The source certificate applies to the frozen tag, not subsequent main development.

Independent verification downloaded all five GitHub assets, checked API digests and signed checksums, verified the archive commit and its installer/changelog contents, and confirmed both Linux architectures carry the tagged revision. Exact-tag image signature and SLSA provenance passed. The version image retained its independently verified candidate index `sha256:6107911e5001651ef78675296de07178da6f778dd44f86845147c56341ed8910`; `latest` resolves to that same index. All five public npm tarballs passed identity, version and integrity checks. Normal npm execution outside the repository with a new cache returned `0.18.16`; its temporary directory was removed. Evidence: `.temp_files/release-01816-6fa1046b/artifact-verification-state.json`.

The versioned-image normal-deploy artifact independently retained **1,894 HTTP 200 responses**, zero unexpected errors/502, across HTTP (503), strict HTTP (342), TCP (343), running (376) and command (330). Each trace contains responses from both the previous and replacement generation; owned-fixture cleanup was confirmed. Its source CI counterpart retained 1,882 HTTP 200 responses. Evidence: `.temp_files/release-01816-6fa1046b/independent-release-runtime-verification.json` and the CI counterpart.

The primary-network regression also passed on the signed versioned image: five topologies and all 15 readiness decisions agreed with real Traefik. Healthy controls returned 60 HTTP 200 responses; detached-primary and private-listener fault controls deliberately returned 40 proxy 502 responses and were refused by readiness. In [comparison 41301478855](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41301478855), the unchanged digest-pinned 0.18.15 image falsely reported ready five times across those two unreachable topologies; the candidate refused all of them. Both comparison fixtures and versioned-image fixtures were removed. Four Go-template cases and four address regressions failed before the first fix; selected-address/stability checks failed before the second. The covering eight-file suite passed 228 tests. These direct admission and isolated traffic checks do not certify a production DNS/TLS cutover or complete the wider R2 matrix.

The signed versioned-image PostgreSQL autoscaling trace independently retained 2,407 HTTP 200 responses, all carrying SQL value 42. The service scaled 1→2→1 and both new immutable replicas served. Owned-fixture cleanup was confirmed. This accepts the stated single-node memory metric and PostgreSQL configuration, not RPS scaling or every runtime topology. Evidence: `.temp_files/release-01816-6fa1046b/release-autoscale-database/independent-verification.json`.

After the frozen tag, [PR #6](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/pull/6) fixed a packaged-desktop smoke race: a Chromium target may appear before its launcher preload is ready. The smoke now waits for both form and isolated bridge on first launch and restart. All 27 local desktop tests and typecheck passed; [three-platform packaged/installed acceptance](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41305018506) and [full source/runtime CI](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41305018615) passed on `2a37c05e` before merge. This harness change is outside v0.18.16. The tag's original macOS smoke passed failed-job retry after the initial preload-timing failure; no numbered tag or image was replaced.

The [0.18.15 release workflow](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41289832315) completed successfully, including all seven published-image smoke cohorts, promotion and all five npm publications. Its initial image job passed the source and backup gates; a stalled workflow was cancelled and resumed with failed-job retry, preserving the already verified candidate index `sha256:4237e24eeb01ec5d5fe3055fe7b1e03efd53f2221f521a5f20c4e5c848e33173`. The successful [source CI](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41289836391) executed 17,769 tests in 1,123 files; all eight test tasks ran, while four build dependencies were cached. The merged main tree matched the tag exactly; subsequent development commits are outside this certificate.

Independent publication verification downloaded all five GitHub assets, checked their digests and signed checksums, verified the archive commit and its installer/changelog contents, and confirmed both Linux image architectures carry the tagged revision. Image signature and SLSA provenance passed with the exact tag/source identity; `latest` resolves to the same index. All five public npm tarballs passed integrity/version checks. The CLI initially returned a transient registry metadata 404 after publication; ordinary metadata then became available and a fresh npm execution outside the repository, with a separate empty cache, returned `0.18.15`. The temporary execution directory was removed. Evidence: `.temp_files/release-01815-f2c282d1/artifact-verification-state.json` and its downloaded assets/logs.

The published-image normal-deploy acceptance independently retained 1,945 HTTP 200 responses across HTTP, strict HTTP, TCP, running and command readiness, with no unexpected error/502 and confirmed owned-fixture cleanup. The equivalent source CI additionally passed all 11 canary cases (10,052 requests; zero unexpected errors/502, with 354 deliberately injected business-error 503 responses) and PostgreSQL autoscaling (2,685 successful responses carrying SQL value 42; both new immutable replicas served). These are the stated isolated scenarios, not a production DNS/TLS cutover or completion of R2's wider runtime matrix.

The v0.18.14 tag remains on `eddf9a64281cb71c991a88951b57e3023396e9ef`. [Release run 41254561302](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41254561302) passed the full source gate (12 tasks, four cached build dependencies; all eight test tasks ran), backup integration and signed multi-architecture image publication. Six smoke cohorts passed. Public canary reached the owner-disabled refusal, which correctly failed the deployment and retained the stable service, but its traffic collector had fewer than 20 samples when stopped. That assertion blocked promotion and npm publication. The tag is not a GitHub Release. The normal panel health artifact independently contains 1,888 HTTP 200 responses across all five modes and confirms owned-fixture cleanup. Evidence: `.temp_files/release-01814-eddf9a64/`.

The 0.18.15 smoke harness waits for a marker written after 20 actual collected outcomes before submitting any canary deployment. A 30-second baseline deadline refuses to proceed without collection; early 502 responses remain in the final trace and still fail acceptance. Two regression assertions failed before the patch; three focused collector tests now pass, including the deadline control. The covering five-file suite passed 51 tests and server typecheck passed. The hosted CI and published-image confirmation are recorded above; the prior fast-refusal case collected 63 samples in CI without starting a candidate. Normal CI now also runs the public canary lifecycle, retaining synthetic traffic traces; final release diagnostics retain those traces on failure.

R2 node autoscaling now prepares immutable serving and spare containers during eligible deployments, confirms node readiness and routing, and fences scale decisions against deployment, lifecycle and database attachment changes. On development commit `c08fde7edff19f4613240ff65856997dbf3b03f5`, [GitHub Actions run 41129661473](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/41129661473) passed the isolated public-API memory autoscaling smoke: one serving replica scaled to two and back to one, both immutable replicas served through Traefik, and all 2,550 monitored requests returned HTTP 200. The runner's owned containers, volumes and network were removed. The same run passed real Docker/PostgreSQL integration, but its overall CI failed on two migration-test lint errors; the subsequent correction and CI run are separate evidence. This focused smoke does not cover production DNS/TLS, node autoscaling with a database, RPS, sleep/wake, fan-out or all R2 acceptance. Artifact: `ci-node-autoscale-41129661473` (local copy: `.temp_files/gh-node-autoscale-41129661473/`).

The [v0.18.12 release](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/releases/tag/v0.18.12) points to `757fc8edd38a9ea94e54a64a1e6d4173ffdba94f`. Its uncached Linux `release:check` passed 17,179 tests, exact-commit GitHub CI passed, and all seven published-image smoke groups passed, including upgrade, node resource limits, database pooling and Swarm routing/file-secret updates. The completed release workflow published the GitHub assets and five npm packages. Independent checks verified the source archive commit, asset checksums and signature, signed amd64/arm64 image identities, npm tarball integrity and the normally downloaded CLI reporting 0.18.12. A cached npm tarball 404 cleared after its 300-second cache lifetime. Evidence: `.temp_files/release-01812-757fc8ed/`. Public DNS/TLS, production traffic and the wider R2 acceptance remain separate work.

R2 development has a separate sealed `docker.startSet` capability for starting pre-existing managed replicas by immutable ID under the shared journal revision. It preflights every target, confirms the resulting state and refuses an old request after a newer fence. A local compiled image passed 11 private-Docker scenarios through independent sealed agent processes, including Start receipt replay, a newer Stop, and same-name replacement safety. The smoke fixture verifies its random owner label and immutable container identity before host-resource cleanup. Evidence: `.temp_files/startset-real-20261030/`. This was agent-protocol evidence only; the newer public autoscaling proof is recorded above.

On source commit `ae921a0d`, an isolated local image passed 13 private-Docker agent scenarios, including sealed inventory watermark enforcement and ordered proxy-write fencing. A separate controller fixture on the same image prepared a running replica and two stopped spares, recovered a lost Start receipt, scaled down, and rejected the stale Start using real Docker and SQLite. Its routing and readiness callbacks were test doubles; it did not exercise a public panel or sealed HTTP. Both accepted runs reported no remaining labelled test containers or volumes. Evidence: `.temp_files/autoscale-agent-ae921a0d-20261030/` and `.temp_files/autoscale-controller-proof-ae921a0d-20261030/`. The later public proof above covers its stated readiness and routing gaps only for the tested configuration.

The [v0.18.11 release](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/releases/tag/v0.18.11) points to `1b69b62d0ecda7269c81039fc1c14c8f9706bf53`. Its clean Linux `release:check`, exact-commit GitHub CI, release workflow and six published-image smoke groups passed, including two initial-deploy Stops followed by a successful deploy. The release archive and installer matched `SHA256SUMS`, and all five npm packages became available. The public smoke uses an isolated HTTP fixture; production DNS/TLS and broader R2 acceptance remain separate work.

After v0.18.11, initial Stop and completed-Stop recovery preflight every participant and identify agents older than 0.18.11 before attempting a handoff. The Stop remains held with an update reason. A local public API/worker smoke paired the candidate panel with the actual v0.18.10 agent image and confirmed the candidate container was not stopped; a second smoke passed two Stop/redeploy cycles using the updated agent. Evidence: `.temp_files/public-old-agent-permanent-20261030/` and `.temp_files/public-initial-after-mixed-20261030/`. The v0.18.12 release workflow includes this mixed-agent scenario; production DNS/TLS remains unverified.

The v0.18.0 tag and image remain available as an unpublished candidate. The hosted smoke caught a setup race: readiness was changed during primary retirement, so the safety journal retained both generations and held the next deployment. The corrected smoke waits for settlement before the next readiness case. The 0.18.1 tag was also withheld after a repeated real canary smoke exposed agent operation capacity exhaustion; its workflow was cancelled before producing a registry image. Commit d8615abc separates bounded operation capacity from the invalid-request rejection budget. Published 0.18.2 preserves both earlier Git tags and the v0.18.0 image.

## Normal panel deploy healthcheck traffic acceptance — 2026-10-31

A real fixture used migrated SQLite, two independent private Docker daemons, sealed HTTP agents and two Traefik instances. All seven scenarios passed: complete multi-node Start; ordered Restart; primary-ready/child-HTTP-404 refusal and recovery; offline-child Stop and same-command recovery; a lost child effect receipt replayed against exact immutable identities; a newer Stop superseding a real child Start callback; and a lost child routing response requiring fresh readiness on both nodes without replaying Start. It invokes the production controller/runtime, not public lifecycle HTTP endpoints, and advances retry scheduling explicitly rather than claiming real backoff elapsed. The public route is covered separately by the permanent API regression. No public DNS/TLS or production traffic was tested.

The fixture's first attempts were setup diagnostics: a literally escaped YAML newline, a check image without the Docker CLI, and an insufficient five-second fixture readiness budget. The accepted fixture uses a fifteen-second service budget without changing production readiness or sample requirements. The refusal test's wording assertion was corrected to the actual unencrypted-transport explanation. None of these diagnostics is counted as a product RED or acceptance. All owned runtime containers, networks and volumes were removed. The clean runtime has exactly the same 2,535 compiled files as the checked build, with no changed, missing or extra files, and cold-starts as UID 999 with healthy application/database status. An earlier COPY overlay retained 57 old web assets; the clean image explicitly removes its old compiled directories before copying the checked build.

The first complete check stopped at web function coverage: all web tests passed, but 97.48% missed the unchanged 97.5% floor. Commit 4e69ebcd adds a behavioral routing refresh test: a refused observation remains visible, refresh stays disabled while pending, and the resulting container/domain/IPv6 allow-list route replaces the error. Its three focused tests pass. The final frozen `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm release:check` passed **15,066 tests in 899 files, no failures or skips, all 11 final tasks uncached**. Typecheck, lint, build and every existing coverage floor passed. Server coverage was 93.25% statements, 87.94% branches, 91.35% functions and 96.35% lines; web coverage was 98.09%, 94.09%, 97.50% and 98.64% respectively. This accepts source 899fa966 plus 5ab886ef / 4e69ebcd / de3ec37d, with all twelve frozen owned inputs matching their committed normalized blobs. The disposable check container removes only its own `/.dockerenv` marker to exercise existing native-host installation assumptions; no source, threshold or test selection is weakened. All 2,535 artifacts rebuilt during the successful gate also match the clean runtime byte for byte. Hosted CI remains a separate gate. Evidence: .temp_files/r2-fanout-ordering-20261025-41ee49e6/verification-state.json.

R2/0.19.0 remain open. Next is Stop during an unresolved fan-out generation handoff, followed by shared deploy/scale/wake ordering, local-primary fan-out, stopped autoscale capacity and network/mount acceptance, node autoscale/sleep/wake, the actual Swarm support matrix, mixed-agent upgrades and final publication gates. R3–R6 remain separate future releases. The published stable remains 0.18.2; these development commits do not publish 0.19.0.


## Stop across retained generations: agent protocol and builder ordering — 2026-10-26

Commit 66eee027 adds the development agent capability docker.lifecycle.generations. An explicit Stop batch supplies the expected deployment label for every immutable container ID/name. The agent validates the complete batch before any Docker effect, checks it again afterward and persists one service revision and replayable receipt for every generation together. Explicit Stop batches are bounded at thirty targets; implicit legacy batches retain their ten-target limit. Start rejects explicit generation annotations. The existing NINEDEPLOY_AGENT_CONTAINER_LIFECYCLE switch disables both capabilities. Legacy Stop cannot mutate any generation adopted in that receipt, while the existing unrelated older-generation retirement control still passes. The panel also refuses target generation annotations not present in its request.

The original agent proof failed the new mixed-generation case while its 31 existing controls passed. A separate real-Docker reproduction confirmed that both generation-9 and generation-10 containers and a foreign-service decoy were running before the old protocol refused the Stop. On the corrected source, all eight real-Docker cases passed independently on Node 22.23.4, 24.22.1 and 26.12.1: 24 runtime checks. They cover one-revision Stop of both generations without stopping the foreign service, a fresh-process durable retry after an obsolete target is removed, same-name replacement protection, generation/service-label refusal, older or explicitly mixed Start refusal, legacy Stop fences for both adopted generations, and owner-disabled refusal before journal or Docker effects. These invoke the production registered agent operation with a sealed context, not actual sealed HTTP or the public panel controller. All owned daemons, runners and journal volumes were removed. The permanent smoke is included in the release workflow.

All 626 schema tests passed with unchanged 100% statement, branch, function and line floors. The related Linux suite passed 224 tests in nine files. The initial receipt fixture used a Start response, which the new protocol correctly rejects before the panel comparison; the corrected Stop fixture exercises that comparison itself. A full diagnostic then exposed the missing human-readable feature entry in the old-agent refusal test registry: 10,526 server tests passed and that new generated case failed. Commit 1766fe86 completes the exhaustive fixture; all 51 refusal tests pass, with the original version/message/only-ping assertions preserved. No threshold or test selection was weakened.

The final acceptance snapshot includes the concurrently committed Doctor changes in 819bd5bd and matches committed source 1766fe86. Its combined capability, lifecycle, Doctor and OpenAPI checks passed 220 tests in seven files. The final frozen `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm release:check` passed **15,083 tests in 899 files, no failures or skips, all 11 final tasks uncached**, on committed source 1766fe86. Typecheck, lint, build and all existing floors passed. Server coverage was 93.27% statements, 87.98% branches, 91.38% functions and 96.36% lines; web coverage was 98.09%, 94.09%, 97.50% and 98.64%. The disposable check container removes only its own `/.dockerenv` marker for existing native-host installation assumptions; source, thresholds and selection remain unchanged. The immutable checked-build image and complete runtime match in all 2,535 compiled files. Post-run container collection was unavailable because the successful terminal container was no longer present; no post-run artifact equivalence is claimed. Hosted CI and publication remain separate gates. The final complete runtime copies every checked package, including web assets changed by the shared capability enum; earlier server/schema-only packaging left 115 web differences and is not accepted as complete artifact identity. The combined runtime separately repeats all eight Docker cases and a UID-999 healthy cold start. Evidence: .temp_files/r2-generation-stop-20261026-6456a11e/verification-state.json.

Panel integration remains open because a second proof reproduces a real ordering defect. A multi-network docker.runSpec operation creates a container and pauses before its raw Docker Start. An ordered Stop then acknowledges that captured ID as stopped; resuming the builder starts it afterward. The isolated production-operation/SQLite fixture fails that assertion while its two neighboring controls pass. A separate real-Docker, independent-process replay confirms created -> complete Stop receipt -> running after builder resume; a subsequent ordinary Stop works as its positive control. The wrapper pauses only immediately before the real Docker Start. It changes no product module. Neither proof is counted as a fixed defect, and neither is inserted as a failing test into the passing main suite. Its evidence and cleaned runtime receipts are retained under late-start-proof/ and late-start-real/ in the same evidence directory.

The next required implementation is one persistent mutation owner shared by deployment creation, network attachment, Start, Stop, scale and wake. Stop must fence and drain older builder work before discovering identities or completing, and a legitimate newer deployment must retain its authorized creation path. Then the parent controller can capture every retained generation, withdraw and acknowledge routing on every node, stop the complete immutable set and settle its handoff journal. Keep the current unresolved-transition hold until both the real late-Start proof and the public panel cancellation/recovery matrix pass. This agent increment does not close R2, publish 0.19.0, or accept R3–R6. The published stable remains 0.18.2.


## Shared runtime authority foundation — 2026-10-26

Migration 0102 adds a private, persistent service runtime owner shared by the declared deploy, lifecycle, scale, sleep/wake and remove mutation kinds. Reservations compare the captured owner and advance one bounded clock; duplicate reservations replay without advancing it, and a stale job cannot reclaim a newer owner. The clock survives lifecycle-history deletion and is retained until the service itself is deleted. The migration preserves the legacy AUTOINCREMENT high-water mark and pending command metadata and keeps already-issued wire revisions unchanged. Malformed snapshots and corrupt or exhausted ownership clocks are retained for review instead of being silently reset.

Node Start/Stop/Restart now reserve that owner in the same transaction as their command. Lease checkpoints, retries and public current/retryable status verify it. A different mutation reservation invalidates the older lifecycle continuation even when placement and desired status did not change. Start/Restart also refuse an unresolved additional-node handoff before taking its authority. The reservation helper alone changes no service status, placement or container state. Production deployment creation, scale, sleep/wake and removal have not yet adopted this authority; their declared kinds and tests are a foundation, not accepted end-to-end integration. The proven late raw runSpec Start remains unfixed and the unresolved-transition hold remains required.

The related Linux suite passed **232 tests in eight files**, including 31 new owner boundary/compatibility cases. All **65 database tests in 21 files** passed at unchanged 100% statement, branch, function and line floors; this includes a real 0101-to-0102 migration with pending commands, deleted history, malformed JSON, replay and cascading deletion. Schema generation reported no additional migration. A Windows diagnostic hit V8 allocation failures and is not counted as acceptance. The first full Linux gate stopped at the new migration test cleanup guard in finally; validation now occurs before the protected cleanup, with no lint suppression or weaker assertion.

The exact production runtime passed **20 real Docker scenarios on Node 26.12.1**: six direct dispatcher cases through sealed HTTP/SQLite/Traefik, seven two-daemon controller cases, and seven public API/worker lifecycle cases. These include actual readiness refusal, immutable effects, route confirmation/drain, hard termination, lost replies, same-command recovery and redeploy after manual lifecycle commands. The direct dispatcher waits for its persisted retry backoff; the multi-node fixture advances retry scheduling explicitly. Public DNS/TLS, production traffic and the delayed raw builder race are not accepted by those smokes. All 2,539 compiled files and 180 migration assets match the checked build byte for byte. The runtime cold-started as UID 999 with HTTP 200 and healthy application/database status; its first unconfigured JWT attempt is retained as a setup diagnostic.

The final frozen `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm release:check` passed **15,115 tests in 901 files, no failures or skips, all 11 final tasks uncached**, certifying committed code 1b9d0370. Typecheck, lint, build and all existing coverage floors passed. Server coverage was 93.27% statements, 88.01% branches, 91.39% functions and 96.36% lines; web coverage was 98.09%, 94.08%, 97.50% and 98.64%. The disposable check container removes only its own `/.dockerenv` marker for existing native-host installation assumptions; no source, threshold or test selection was weakened. All 2,539 compiled files and 180 migration assets copied from the successfully terminated gate also match the production runtime with zero changed, missing or extra files. Hosted [CI for 1b9d0370](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/40300899342) had passed Docker/PostgreSQL integration and image build when local acceptance completed; its full hosted gate was still running then. Hosted completion and publication remain separate requirements.

Next: add a persistent agent mutation guard covering the complete create/network/Start and retirement sequence; bind primary and additional-node builders to the persisted authority without denying a legitimate newer deployment; make both retained late-Start proofs pass; then integrate complete-generation Stop and settle the parent handoff under that same authority. Remaining R2 autoscale/sleep/wake, local-primary fan-out, network/mount, Swarm, mixed-agent and publication gates stay open. R3–R6 remain separate future releases; the published stable remains 0.18.2. Evidence: `.temp_files/r2-runtime-owners-20261026-4959edfa/`.


## Admitted creation drain and child closure — 2026-10-26

Commit 35eb0b01 puts already-admitted managed runSpec and runEnv work under the same per-service native SQLite guard as ordered lifecycle effects. The guard spans create, network attachment, Start and failure cleanup. A timed-out caller keeps its queued work and lock until the underlying child closes. The process helper now waits for close after timeout or a post-spawn error, preserves exit 124 for a timed-out child even if its later exit code is zero, and leaves SIGKILL escalation armed. True spawn failures still return 127. Other service keys remain independent and legitimate newer deployments retain their compatibility path.

The original creation source failed all three new ordering cases while four controls passed. The original timeout helper failed three closure tests while fifteen controls passed. An isolated real Node child ignored SIGTERM: the original helper returned timeout and allowed its successor while that child was still alive. The corrected helper waits for actual closure after SIGKILL. The covering suite passed **206 tests in nine files independently on Windows and Linux**. These are related checks, not global coverage.

The permanent creation smoke passed three real-Docker/native-SQLite scenarios through independent agent processes: multi-network runSpec, single-network runSpec and runEnv. Each pauses immediately before a real Docker mutator, proves that the fence waits for the admitted creator, discovers its immutable identity after the fence, completes Stop without resurrection, and starts a legitimate newer deployment. The same fixture failed against the prior runtime because its fence acknowledged the paused creator immediately. A fourth case uses the production process helper with an isolated executable substitution and a real SIGTERM-resistant Node child; it is process evidence, not an additional Docker service scenario. The smoke is now a release gate. These invoke registered production operations with a sealed context; they do not exercise sealed HTTP or public lifecycle endpoints themselves.

Separate exact-runtime fixtures passed **seven public API/worker lifecycle cases and seven two-node sealed-HTTP/SQLite/Traefik controller cases**. The initial host drivers disappeared before completion; their partial outputs are retained as diagnostics and not accepted. After owned-resource cleanup, independent tracked drivers completed with exit zero and persisted their receipts. Public DNS/TLS and production traffic were not tested. The production runtime cold-started as UID 999 with HTTP 200 and healthy application/database status. All **2,539 compiled files and 180 migration assets** copied from the successfully terminated full gate match that runtime byte for byte.

The uncached frozen `TURBO_FORCE=true pnpm release:check` on committed code 35eb0b01 passed **15,127 tests in 902 files, no failures or skips, all 11 final tasks uncached**. Typecheck, lint, build and all unchanged coverage floors passed. Server coverage was 93.28% statements, 88.01% branches, 91.42% functions and 96.37% lines; web coverage was 98.09%, 94.08%, 97.50% and 98.64%. The disposable gate removes only its own `/.dockerenv` marker for existing host-install assumptions; no source, threshold or selection was weakened. Its original host log stopped before the final result; the terminal Docker container exited zero and supplied the recovered complete log. No suite was restarted to recover observation. Hosted [CI for 35eb0b01](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/40305799681) also completed successfully, including real Docker/PostgreSQL integration and image build.

The remaining ordering boundary is a stale request that reaches the agent only after the newer Stop has completed. A creation lock cannot distinguish that request from a legitimate newer deployment without an explicit persisted authority. Next is typed admission for immutable batch preparation, fencing and retirement, binding all production callers to the shared owner, and full retained-generation handoff settlement. Keep the current unresolved-transition hold until those delayed-request and public recovery cases pass. Remaining R2 autoscale/sleep/wake, local-primary fan-out, networks/mounts, Swarm, mixed-agent and publication gates stay open. R3–R6 remain separate future releases; stable remains 0.18.2. Evidence: `.temp_files/r2-agent-creation-drain-20261026-31b578b8/verification-state.json`.

## Agent absence evidence: real runtime check — 2026-10-28

A disposable derivative of `ninedeploy-proof:r2-prepare-replay-final-20261027`, with the compiled agent absence and mutation modules from `9aeb7230`, completed `smoke:runtime-mutations` with exit 0. All ten scenarios passed using an isolated Docker daemon, native SQLite, sealed HTTP and independent agent processes. They include a delayed older preparation refused after Stop, a later typed deployment accepted, Stop over multiple generations and the fence draining an admitted Start. Evidence: `.temp_files/agent-absence-proof/runtime/cases.json`; derivative image ID: `sha256:d187f6b749afed80a95656adcf74e2d8c67d7b63c37431288d51455bcf835ec6`.

This is agent protocol evidence, not a full build of the current source, a published image, public-panel integration or production traffic. Normal deploy and fan-out still require the ordered producer integration; the previously reproduced Stop race remains open. The uncached release check on `73157601` failed its unchanged server statement coverage floor (93.19% against 93.25%) despite 11,032 passing server tests; the later agent changes were not included in that run.

## Readiness deadline and receipt validation — 2026-10-28

Commit `5327d775` rejects readiness received after the deadline or after ownership is lost, and requires an unambiguous successful node probe for the requested protocol and HTTP status. The local Docker and node/fan-out regression suites passed, including the complete 259-test pipeline file and 44 Swarm/native recovery tests after correcting their simulated Docker missing-container responses. The permanent `smoke:local-docker-readiness` exercises fast and slow HTTP responses for both explicit and default panel readiness and an ownership change; the release workflow runs it against its pushed image.

A disposable derivative image (`sha256:4a33bdd0d366b004f175a296c0f801d670a9776843822be96b91a486844d22c4`) with the updated server and corresponding schema/database outputs completed the real-Docker user journey with exit 0. Its canary held at 50% while 30/30 requests were served with no 5xx, promoted successfully, then retained the previous release through a cancelled canary with 5/5 requests served. The journey also verified scale-up/down, and intentionally received a 503 for a wake request whose client must retry. Evidence: `.temp_files/agent-absence-proof/readiness-user-journey-v2.log`. An earlier partial overlay failed to boot due to mismatched schema exports; it was corrected before this run and is not accepted as proof.

These checks are for a derivative fixture, not the final release image, public DNS/TLS or production traffic. The real-Docker agent readiness smoke also passed four cases on a separate derivative. Default node readiness without an explicit HTTP/TCP mode remains container-state based. The node deploy/Stop ordering race and the final exact-commit release and hosted publication checks remain open.

## Stop during an unselected node deployment — 2026-10-29

The `v0.18.9` tag points to `5e9a329dcdf697cdece7b7db2e2e4734e017970e`; its published candidate image has index digest `sha256:c1c0b0c427b004abfbe129f03bd1deb1de1816639125cd3bdcc868c150068b20`. This is an image candidate, not a GitHub Release. [Release workflow 40939573409](https://github.com/ninedeploy/ninedeploy/actions/runs/40939573409) failed its public-canary and replica-database Stop scenarios and skipped promotion and npm publication. Upgrade, user-journey, Compose restore, agent and panel lifecycle cohorts passed in that run.

Both failures were reproduced on the same candidate image in isolated local Docker daemons. In the replica case the Stop command completed and the selected old replicas stopped, while both cancelled candidate replicas remained running. The cancelled deployment log states that node deployment authority changed and runtime effects were retained for the new owner. In the public canary case the stopped candidate likewise remained running. Local evidence is retained under `.temp_files/replica-v0189-diagnostics-20261029/` and `.temp_files/canary-v0189-repro-20261029/`; these are isolated fixtures, not production traffic.

The unfinished regression `apps/server/test/lib/nodeLifecycleStopCandidate.test.ts` reproduces the selected-runtime case through the durable controller with two candidate replicas and a foreign-service control. On the current source it fails because both candidates remain running after Stop reports completion. On Node 26.12.1, the existing lifecycle intent, controller and runtime mutation suites passed 137 tests; the new regression was the one failure. This is a focused result, not a release gate.

Stop must durably take ownership of all affected immutable generations, drain or fence admitted creation, remove the cancelled candidates without mutating a foreign service or a newer generation, and retain enough state for retry after a crash. Production deploy creation must use the ordered mutation protocol before its fence can safely reject delayed old requests without rejecting future valid deploys. Verify the unchanged regression and both real-Docker public scenarios, including a delayed old create and a later legitimate deploy, before claiming this race fixed or promoting another release.

The development safeguard records interrupted deployment IDs in the Stop snapshot and holds a selected Stop after routing removal and selected-generation shutdown, rather than declaring completion before candidate cleanup. Repeated Stop retains those IDs; Start and later deployment admission wait for the unresolved handoff. A local derivative of the candidate image containing the four changed server modules confirmed the Stop remains in `applying` after the real PostgreSQL replica scenario, while both candidate replicas still run. The unchanged smoke failed because completion did not occur; it did not pass or prove cleanup. Evidence: `.temp_files/replica-stop-hold-proof-20261029/`. This safeguard cannot settle the handoff by itself and is not an acceptable release replacement for ordered candidate retirement and subsequent legitimate deploy acceptance.

The agent now records the highest deployment identity covered by an accepted lifecycle Stop under the same durable service lock used for managed creation. Later legacy creation at or below that identity is refused, even after a newer Start changes the lifecycle head; a later deployment identity remains admissible. A stale lifecycle request cannot advance the recorded boundary. Against the original `v0.18.9` image the extended real-Docker smoke failed because a delayed stopped generation started; a derivative with the three modified agent modules passed all three creation modes, using independent agent processes and native SQLite, and admitted a later generation. The existing drain and process-timeout controls also passed. Evidence: `.temp_files/agent-stale-create-red-20261029/` and `.temp_files/agent-stale-create-green-20261029/`. These are local agent proofs, not sealed HTTP, public-panel acceptance, an upgrade matrix or release artifacts. The panel still needs to fence the complete interrupted generation range and retire its candidates before completing Stop; the held-handoff guard remains in place.

For a selected Stop that interrupts a deployment, the panel now persists the deployment sequence high-water mark, including IDs whose rows were already deleted, and sends that boundary in the initial lifecycle fence. It requires the explicitly advertised `docker.lifecycle.creationFence` capability before the handoff; an old agent keeps the command held. Ordinary selected Stop without an in-flight deployment retains its existing agent compatibility. This is panel/agent contract coverage only: panel-side retirement and automatic settlement are not implemented, and no full public Stop or release acceptance is claimed.

The development agent also exposes a sealed `docker.lifecycleRetire` operation bound to an acknowledged Stop revision and immutable target IDs. Its durable retirement intent refuses changed target sets and a later lifecycle owner; removal is checked before and after the Docker effect and an exact retry tolerates a previously removed ID. A real-Docker RED on the original candidate image reported the operation unavailable; a derivative containing the changed agent/schema modules passed the expanded generation smoke, including foreign-container protection, process-independent retry, a same-name replacement and rejection after a newer revision. Evidence: `.temp_files/agent-lifecycle-retire-red-20261029/` and `.temp_files/agent-lifecycle-retire-green-final-20261029/`. This proves the agent operation, not panel integration: the public Stop still holds until the controller discovers, stops and retires candidate identities, and no release has been promoted.

The selected-runtime Stop controller now freezes candidate names and placements, fences the pre-Stop deployment range, confirms all immutable identities, stops selected and candidate generations together and retires only candidates under the same acknowledged Stop. A lost or invalid retirement receipt holds the command for an idempotent retry. The prior failing controller regression passes, including lost-reply and unavailable-agent cases; two-node selected and unselected target shapes have focused controller tests. In a local derivative image, the public panel/worker/agent canary smoke passed eleven cases, including explicit Stop and panel crash, with 10,509 sampled requests and no unexpected 502. An independent PostgreSQL replica smoke passed Stop during readiness, removed both candidates, then deployed two new replicas and served 30 successful requests. Evidence: `.temp_files/public-stop-handoff-final-20261029/` and `.temp_files/replica-stop-redeploy-20261029/`. The image is a derivative of the tagged candidate and does not certify the final commit, hosted release, public DNS/TLS or the two-node physical path. Initial deployment before any selected runtime and wider node mutation ordering remain separate acceptance work.
